This judgment is the outcome of the final report filed by the PI of Halsuru Gate Police Station,
Bengaluru against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable U/s. 304(A), 337 and 338 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.

2. Brief Facts Of The Case Of Prosecution:-
The case of prosecution is that, accused No.1 is the owner of Madhu Agency and the accused No.2 is the manager of the said agency.
Accused No.3 and 4 are the workers/employees of the said Madhu Agency which supplies C.C. No.29990/2021 LPG Gas.
The deceased by name Krishnashetty was the customer of said Madhu Agency under customer No.444693.

On 07.07.2021 at about 2.00 pm in the house of 1 st floor building No.10, TRS Lane, Nagara pet the customer Krishnashetty had filed a complaint before the Madhu Gas Agency for non supply of gas cylinder.

The accused No.1, 3 and 4 without taking necessary precautions in repair of the gas cylinder and without sending any proper expert to deal with such issue, the accused No.2 was sent for repair of the gas cylinder.

It is further alleged that, when the deceased insisted the accused No.2 to change the cylinder, the accused No.2 negligently and being irresponsible did not change the cylinder and left open the LPG gas cylinder in the house.

As a result the LPG cylinder blast and the deceased Krishnashetty suffered 40% of burn injuries and succumbed to the said injuries on 15.07.2021 at 12.08 hours at St. John Medical Hospital, Bengaluru.
CW.2 sustained fracture injuries to her right hand and CW.2 sustained 25% burn injuries.
The CW.3 sustained 36% burn injuries on her body and CW.4 sustained 18 % burn injuries as well as grievous head injuries in the said blast.

It is further alleged that, the C.C.
No.29990/2021 aforesaid incident occurred due to the negligence of accused No.1 to 4 and thereby the accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention have committed the alleged offences punishable under Sections 304(A), 337 and 338 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.

On the basis of the materials on record the following points arise for the consideration:-
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 being the owner of Madhu Agency, accused No.2 being the manager and accused No.3 and 4 being the workers, on 07.07.2021 at 2.00pm in the house of 1st floor building No.10 TRS Lane, Nagarpet, with common intention had negligently and irresponsibly did not change the cylinder due to which the LPG gas burst causing death of Krishnashetty and thereby committed an offense punishable u/sec. 304(A)
r/w 34 of IPC?
C.C. No.29990/2021 2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that due to the negligent act of accused No.1 to 4, the CW.1 to CW.4 suffered burn injuries and grievous injuries and thereby accused have committed an offense punishable u/sec. 337 and 338 r/w 34 of IPC?
3. What order?
9. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 & 2 :- In the Negative Point No.3 :- As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10 REASONING ON POINT NO.1 AND 2 :- The offences alleged against the accused No.1 to 4 are punishable under Sections 304(A), 337 and 338 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
Sec-304(A). Causing death by negligence- Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Sec-337. Causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others - Whoever causes hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
Sec-338. Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others - Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished C.C. No.29990/2021 with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

In the cross-examination, the PW.3 has stated that on 06.06.2021 they have got the defective cylinder and that MO.1 stove was purchased around 5 years back.

35. In this case, PW.1 to PW.4 are the injured victims.

All the PW.1 to PW.4 have deposed that,
accused No.2 had come to their house.
They have also stated that, a new filled cylinder was supplied to them on 06.07.2021.

On appreciating the entire evidence of PW.1 to PW.4 it can be gathered that on the date of fateful incident i.e., 07.07.2021, a gas cylinder was exhausted, a new cylinder was already C.C. So as per the evidence of PW.1 to PW.4, there was one empty cylinder, one cylinder which is said to be defective and another cylinder which was brought by the accused No.2 in the afternoon to their home.
At this stage, it would be important to go through the contents of mahazar.
The mahazar is marked as Ex.P.2.
In the mahazar it is stated that, the house of Krishnashetty is situated in 1 st floor measuring 15 X 40 feet consisting of one hall, 2 bedrooms, 1 bathroom.
The kitchen is measuring 6 X 10 ft., in the kitchen there is one water filter, one refrigerator.

But as per the evidence of PW.1 to PW.4, there were 3 cylinders at C.C. No.29990/2021 the time of accident i.e., one empty cylinder, one cylinder which is said to be defective and another cylinder which was brought by the accused No.2 in the afternoon to their home.
To bring home the guilt of Gourav K vs Linith Clark on 11 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49557901/
11 the accused beyond reasonable doubt, it was incumbent upon the IO to state in the mahazar about the other two cylinders, which were present at the home at the time of alleged incident.

Even in the mahazar, the Investigating Officer has not mentioned the number of the cylinders, which was seized by him.
The prosecution has produced Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7 i.e., photographs of cylinder.

It is not explained by the prosecution, if the cylinder shown in Ex.P.6 is the same cylinder, which got blast or it is the cylinder which was brought by the accused No.2 or it is the cylinder which got emptied.
The Ex.
P.6 and Ex.P.7 shows some numbers on the cylinder, but in the mahazar the details of said cylinder which was seized from the place of incident is not mentioned.
37. The prosecution has not produced any documentary evidence to show that, on 06.07.2021 a gas cylinder was C.C. No.29990/2021 supplied to the house of deceased.

As the said cylinder is in dispute, it was incumbent upon the Investigating Officer to give the details of the said cylinder,
which was supplied to the house of deceased.
The evidence of PW.1 shows that, deceased Krishnashetty had connected the cylinder to the stove and MO.2 is not identified by the complainant.
Thus, the very important materials object is not identified by the witnesses.
The Ex.P.7 shows that, the said cylinder was intact and even Ex.P.6 shows that the said cylinder was intact.

38. The evidence of Investigating Officer in this case is utmost important, because only on the oral say of PW.1 to PW.4 it cannot be accepted that, the defective cylinder was the sole cause for the fateful incident.
39. Generally, to connect gas cylinder to the stove, a regulator and a pipe is used and to light the stove a lighter or matchbox is used.
Thus, stove, pipe, regulator, cylinder and the lighter or matchbox are necessary objects.
In the presence of all these objects fire can be lit.
As per Ex.P.2 mahazar the Police have not seized the pipe, regulator or the C.C. No.29990/2021 lighter or matchbox from the place of incident.
There is nothing on record to show that, there was no defect in the stove or the regulator or the pipe.
The regulator also plays an important role here, because through the regulator and the pipe only the gas can be flown to the stove to lit the fire.
The Investigating Officer by name Mallikarjun who is examined as PW.11 has done very mechanical and casual investigation in this case.
In the cross-examination, he admits that on 08.07.2021 he visited the spot in the morning and found that the door was damaged and things were scattered.
He admits that, there was a exhaust fan in the kitchen, but the same is not mentioned in the mahazar.
He admits that, there was no window in the kitchen.
If there was no window in the kitchen then where the exhaust fan was fixed is not explained by the prosecution.
He admits that, the batch number of the cylinder is not mentioned in the Ex.P.2.
He also admits that, the gas stove was not sent to the FSL for examining its quality.
He admits that, he has not seized the gas lighter.
He admits that, he has not investigated about the stove and its company.
He further admits that, he has not sent the cylinder to the LPG equipment research center for examining C.C. No.29990/2021 if there was any defect in the said cylinder.
He admits that, in the home there was only one cylinder.
He has deposed that, accused No.2 connected the regulator and lit the stove, but none of the prosecution witnesses have deposed that the regulator was fixed by the accused No.2.
The PW.1 to PW.4 have themselves stated that, deceased had connected the stove regulator to the new cylinder.

12 40.

The prosecution has stated that, agency of the accused was informed about the defective cylinder, but the Investigating Officer has not produced any material documents to show that the accused No.2 was working in the Madhu Agency and that on the said date of incident, he was deputed for working out the defective cylinder in the house of deceased Krishnashetty.
The prosecution has not produced any documents to show that, the family of Krishnashetty had lodged any complaint before the Madhu Agency reporting about the leakage of the gas cylinder.

Even the Investigating Officer has not taken pain of collecting the call history records of the family of complainant or the deceased to prove C.C. No.29990/2021 that on the date of alleged incident, they had reported about the leakage of the gas cylinder.
41.
The CW.2 who is also injured in his evidence has deposed that, the said pipe which was connected to the stove does not belongs to them.

When the CW.2 himself admits that, the said pipe which was connected to the stove does not belongs to them, then it was upon the Investigating Officer to produce the details of the pipe such as number on the pipe or any company details to prove that on the date of alleged incident, the said pipe connected to the stove which is shown in the photograph was belonging to the family of deceased.
42. The Investigating Officer has unequivocally admitted that, he has not sent the cylinder and stove for examination.
In this case, there is a alleged leakage of gas from the cylinder which was fateful to the residents of deceased family.

The Investigating Officer has not explained as to what prevented him from sending the gas cylinder, pipe, regulator and the stove to the expert or FSL to get the expert opinion about the defective objects in this case.

When gas cylinder, stove, regulator, pipe and lighter are the C.C. No.29990/2021 contributing material to lit a fire, it was incumbent upon the Investigating Officer to get the expert opinion in this regard.
Even the photograph of the cylinder shows that, the cylinder was intact.
The Investigating Officer has not conducted proper investigation and took the investigation in a very casual way, which was fatal to the case of prosecution.

43. The learned counsel for the accused argued that, the Madhu Agency is involved in procuring the gas cylinders from the manufacturing company and supplies the same to the customers in accordance with booking.
The Madhu Agency do not fill, refill or undertakes services of the cylinders.

In this regard, the prosecution has not produced any such documentary evidence to show the nature of work of Madhu Agency or to prove that the negligence of the Agency took the life of Krishnashettty and injured his family members.
The Investigating Officer has not even taken the expert opinion by the technician or the expert to prove that the alleged incident occurred due to the defective cylinder.

The oral evidence of prosecution witnesses though has consistency, but taking into consideration the nature of C.C. No.29990/2021 incident and the manner in which incident took place, in the absence of any expert opinion or any report about the defective equipment, it cannot be concluded that the alleged accident took place due to the defective gas cylinder.

The admissions given by the Investigating Officer Sri. Mallikarjuna that he has not noted the batch number of the cylinder at the time of conducting mahazar and at the time of seizure, his admission that he has not sent the gas cylinder for FSL to check the accuracy and quality and his admission he has not sent to the cylinder to the LPG equipment research center to check its accuracy and his admission that there was only one cylinder in the house clearly shows that due to the faulty and weak investigation the case of the prosecution has failed.

13 44.
The prosecution has argued that, the accused No.2 also suffered burn injuries in the said incident and eventually he died.
The seizure mahazar witness has stated that, from last 3 years he is working in Madhu Agency and accused No.3 is the manager and accused No.4 is a gas cylinder delivery boy.

From the statement of said witnesses it C.C. No.29990/2021 is clear that, accused No.2 was not an employee of Madhu Agency, but no documentary evidence is produced by the prosecution to show that, accused No.2 was the employee of the Madhu Agency.
45.
It is pertinent to note that, it is undisputed that the injured and deceased were residing in the 1 st floor of the building.
One of the witness has stated that, the fire might have occurred due to the short circuit or any other reason.
It is undisputed that, there are shops in the ground floor of the building.
Under such circumstances, the Investigating Officer ought to have examined the actual cause of fire by taking the help of experts in this regard.
The PW.16 in his cross- examination has admitted that, he has not taken cylinder from the house of the complainant to the station and that there was no damage in the cylinder, which was open.
He admits that, he applied water on the nozzle and examined the cylinder, which contained the serial number.

From the evidence of PW.16 it can be elicited that, the accused No.2 was not the employee of the agency and also elicited that the Police have taken to 2 cylinders for the purpose of C.C. No.29990/2021 investigation.
The Investigating Officer has not explained as to which cylinder was retained and which cylinder was produced as MO before the Court.
The conduct of the Investigating Officer shows that, he was very negligent in conducting the investigation.
46. Thus, the prosecution has miserably to failed to prove that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the accused persons.

Though the evidence of PW.1 to PW.4 founds some consistency about the accident, but the same is not sufficient with regard to the material objects produced by the Investigating Officer to prove that, the accused are guilty.
It would be justifiable to mention that the prosecution has failed to prove this case because of the faulty, improper and negligent investigation by the Investigating Officer Sri. Mallikarjuna.
Hence, in the absence of cogent documentary evidence the charges levelled against the Accused persons are not proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
47. Thus in the absence of cogent oral and documentary evidence the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the C.C. No.29990/2021 alleged offenses against the Accused.
Hence Point No.1 and 2 are answered in NEGATIVE.

ORDER Acting U/s.248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused No.1, 3 and 4 are hereby Acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.304(A), 337 and 338 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
